reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an educational walkthrough of the creator’s own Uniswap ETH/USDC liquidity position, including reported fees and a calculation based on approximately $99 of deposited capital. Although it highlights a notable yield and invites viewers to try the strategy, it distinguishes past yield from future performance and discloses smart-contract, impermanent-loss, and market-volatility risks. Related paid resources are mentioned, but the available video evidence does not establish deceptive conduct, guaranteed returns, viewer losses, or a harmful connection to the demonstrated position.

opening.argument: The video links a promised income result directly to participating in an ETH/USDC liquidity pool. Viewers are told to pull up their own LP position, double the fees, divide by the deposit, and post the result, while the description presents more than 6% monthly yield from deposited capital. It also directs viewers to a full tutorial so they can try the same activity. That is a concrete participation pathway: deploy capital into the pool, then expect recurring fee income calculated from the deposit. The offer is made especially actionable by presenting a $99.12 example as proof of the concept and saying the same percentage applies even to $100,000.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this educational does not remove the solicitation. The cited wallet and fee history establish that a position existed, but they do not establish that viewers will obtain the promoted yield. The disclaimer likewise does not undo the repeated invitation to open a position, calculate its income, and follow the tutorial. The central viewer-facing message remains that depositing capital can produce more than 6% monthly.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The action language is an invitation to reproduce an openly described demonstration, not proof of a guaranteed reward. The quoted material shows one reported fee result and a suggested calculation, but it does not show that viewers were promised the same result. The speaker expressly states that past yield is not indicative of future performance and discloses that DeFi involves smart-contract risk, impermanent loss, and market volatility.

opening.argument: Several unusually attractive return signals are concentrated around a capital-deployment product. The description leads with over 6% monthly yield, reports $3.16 in fees on $99.12 over 15 days, and says the percentage works the same from $100 to $100,000. The displayed Revert Finance screen also shows a 76.52% total APR and 72.70% fee APR alongside the position and fees earned. Those figures can make a volatile liquidity position look like a straightforward, scalable income engine. The risk language appears only as a disclaimer after the income pitch, while the video continues to say the position is on track to make more than 6% per month.

this particular pool has more than a hundred million dollars in tvl there's plenty of room for big positions

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of a risk disclaimer does not neutralize the prominence of the return signals. A past-performance warning cannot make a 6% monthly projection, a large APR display, and the claim that the math scales to $100,000 cease functioning as an inducement. Nor does a $100 million TVL claim establish that the advertised yield is stable or that large deposits avoid loss.

citations.quote: Past yield is not indicative of future performance.
we're on track to make more than 6% per month on the capital that we deployed into this position.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These figures are presented as observed fees and an explicitly labeled estimate, not as a fixed return. The screen shows a particular position and fee total, while the speaker explains that he doubled 15 days of fees to estimate a month. The material also specifically identifies smart-contract risk, impermanent loss, and market volatility, so the evidence does not show that the position is risk-free or that the APR will persist.

opening.argument: The educational framing functions as promotion because the walkthrough repeatedly moves from explanation to participation. It showcases a live liquidity position, calculates a monthly income figure, says the range performed well, collects the fees, and then invites viewers to try the strategy themselves. The surrounding description expands that funnel beyond a tutorial: it offers a free income course, a strategy call, a paid $97-per-month community, and an accelerator program. In that context, the technical demonstration is not merely neutral instruction. It uses a small personal position, favorable fee math, and apparent proof of ownership to make depositing into the same pool seem like a practical route to DeFi income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The technical detail strengthens the promotional effect rather than disproving it. Showing an NFT, logs, a chart, and fee collection supplies credibility for the same income pitch. The description's strategy call, paid community, accelerator, and income course are not incidental neutral references; they surround a message telling viewers to deploy capital and try the method. Educational labeling therefore describes format, not the practical function of the content.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The surrounding resources do not show that access to them is required to obtain returns, nor do they establish deception. The demonstration identifies the pool, deposit, fee history, range, and collection process so viewers can inspect the mechanics. The speaker also says the result is based on a 15-day period and includes explicit warnings that future performance is not established. Promotion of educational resources is not itself proof of a fraudulent investment scheme.
